source.confidence: high for illustration direction, low for full interface tokens

creative_direction.name: Friendly imperfect ink
creative_direction.emotional_goal: Make the product feel clever, approachable, and made by people rather than a sterile automation system.
creative_direction.visual_thesis: Use a simple black ink character with visible imperfections as the emotional anchor, then keep the surrounding interface quiet so the character carries the personality.
creative_direction.design_tension: Friendly character energy balanced by calm, precise product structure.
do: Preserve asymmetry and hand pressure variation.
Use generous whitespace around character art.
Keep supporting UI restrained and legible.
Use the character as a guide, status marker, or moment of reassurance.
dont: Do not smooth the drawing into a sterile vector icon.
Do not add glossy gradients, 3D rendering, or polished mascot detail.
Do not combine the ink character with a noisy visual theme.
Do not use the character as decoration on every surface.
Do not reduce accessibility contrast for the sake of softness.

ink.usage: primary illustration, primary text, strong borders

paper.usage: illustration background and calm content surfaces

muted_paper.usage: secondary panels, inactive areas, soft separation

signal.usage: status emphasis through weight, not hue

rules: Use color sparingly in the product UI; the reference image is intentionally monochrome.
Maintain at least WCAG AA contrast for interface text.
Use texture or stroke variation for personality, never low contrast.

typography.direction: Friendly humanist sans-serif paired with optional hand-lettered display moments.
rules: Keep letter spacing at zero for display and body text.
Use weight and spacing to create hierarchy instead of extra colors.
Do not use a novelty handwritten font for long-form UI text.

line_quality.cleanup: remove accidental noise only; retain character

rendering.preferred_asset: transparent PNG or high-resolution raster with paper background handled by the UI
rendering.alternate_asset: SVG that preserves rough stroke texture rather than mathematically perfect paths

role_variants.hush: quiet captain, harbor light, or final gate mark

corner_radius.rule: Prefer modest rounding; avoid soft toy-like cards.

spacing.principle: Give the character room to breathe; use tighter spacing for operational data.

composition.preferred: unframed character beside or above a concise message
composition.hero: character first, then product promise, then next action
composition.workflow: character marks at key state transitions, not on every node

character_mark.purpose: humanize an agent, state, or empty state
character_mark.behavior: static by default; use only subtle motion for meaningful state changes

status_card.icon: small character crop or simple ink mark
status_card.rule: Never place a status card inside another card.

primary_action.interaction: invert to paper background with ink text on hover

motion.enter: short ease-out fade with 2px vertical movement
motion.success: subtle hand-drawn wobble or stamp-like settle
motion.error: brief horizontal nudge, never a violent shake
motion.reduced_motion: remove movement and preserve state change through contrast and text

accessibility.contrast: WCAG AA minimum for all UI text
accessibility.alt_text: Describe the character's role or state, not just 'illustration'.
accessibility.meaning: Never communicate status through illustration alone.
accessibility.focus: Use a visible 2px ink focus ring with 2px offset.

implementation_notes.most_important_rule: The interface should feel precise underneath and human on top.
implementation_notes.calibration: The reference image defines the illustration language, not exact UI dimensions or typography.
review_questions: Does the character still look hand-made at the rendered size?
Can a user understand the state without seeing the illustration?
Is the surrounding interface quiet enough for the character to matter?
Did we preserve asymmetry instead of polishing away the personality?
